articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally yeeted AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets onto GitHub, proving once again that the cybersecurity agency tasked with protecting us can't even secure their own repos. Congress is rightfully losing their minds.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA's contractor exposed privileged AWS GovCloud credentials on GitHub because apparently irony is dead and we're all living in a cybersecurity fever dream. The agency that tells everyone else to secure their infrastructure just got pwned by basic OPSEC failure.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from checking school residency to noise complaints, because why solve actual crimes when you can build a surveillance panopticon? Mission creep in action, folks.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Cops are literally stalking social media to spy on people criticizing AI data centers, because apparently having opinions about corporate surveillance infrastructure makes you a threat. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a warrant.

articles.title: Palo Alto VPN bug graduates from advisory to active exploitation
articles.summary: GTA cheat service Atlas Menu got hacked and 64,000 user records dumped after attacker claimed the service was spying via screenshots. Even the cheaters can't trust their cheat providers anymore—what a world.

articles.title: Show HN: Simple news aggregator with source bias meters
articles.summary: Microsoft is threatening security researchers with their 'Digital Crimes Unit' over zero-day disclosures, because nothing says 'we care about security' like intimidating the people who find your bugs. Peak corporate dystopia vibes.

articles.title: California sues 23andMe over large 2023 data breach
articles.summary: Carnival Cruise exposed 6 million customers' data because apparently their security was as leaky as their reputation for stranding people at sea. Another day, another massive breach that could have been prevented.

articles.title: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher Nightmare Eclipse for exploit disclosure
articles.summary: California is suing 23andMe over their 2023 data breach that exposed genetic information, proving that your DNA data is about as secure as your browser history. At least someone's holding these companies accountable.

articles.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-0257) Under Active Exploitation
articles.summary: Microsoft's legal intimidation tactics against researcher Nightmare Eclipse could kill vulnerability research entirely, because who needs security when you have lawyers? This is how we end up with more exploited systems, not fewer.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: CVE-2026-0257 in Palo Alto's PAN-OS GlobalProtect is being actively exploited for authentication bypass, because even the companies that sell security can't secure their own products. Emergency patch Tuesday strikes again.
